prompt:
Triangle X Y Z is shown. Angle Y X Z is a right angle. The length of Y X is 12 inches and the length of X Z is 10 inches. Angle X Y Z is x.
Which is the best approximation for the measure of angle XYZ?

33.6°
39.8°
50.2°
56.4°
judge_reasoning: The user asks: “Which is the best approximation for the measure of angle XYZ?” For this right triangle (right angle at X), tan(∠XYZ)=XZ/YX=10/12=5/6, giving ∠XYZ≈39.8°. Candidate [1] computes this correctly and matches the correct option, while [2] and [4] use the sine ratio with the numerator swapped (leading to 50.2°). Candidate [3] has a more serious geometric/Pythagorean setup error (producing 33.6°).
